title: Waxed Cotton with Ronnie Romance
content:
Join Ronnie Romance inside Halley Stevensons in Dundee, Scotland, to discover how waxed cotton is made and why this centuries-old fabric still has a place in modern outdoor clothing.

The story of waxed cotton begins at sea. In the early 15th century, Scottish herring fishermen began treating their sails with fish oils and grease to protect them from the elements. Worn pieces of sailcloth were later repurposed as capes, helping sailors withstand wind and sea spray.

Since 1864, Halley Stevensons has continued to develop this tradition in Dundee. Today, the process brings together generations of knowledge, industrial machinery and a surprising amount of human touch.

For Ronnie, that is part of the appeal. Waxed cotton is durable, repairable and made to change with use. Marks, creases and patina become part of the fabric, while the surface can be re-waxed to maintain its weather resistance over time.
